what_its_for: Levocetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and itchy skin caused by hay fever (seasonal allergies) or year-round allergies. It is also used to treat chronic hives (urticaria) and relieve itching.
how_to_take: Take levocetirizine by mouth with or without food. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the oral solution (liquid), measure your dose carefully with a medication measuring spoon or syringe — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Take this medicine in the evening, as it works best when taken at the same time each day.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: The usual dose is 5 mg (one tablet or 10 mL of oral solution) once daily in the evening. Children 6 to 11 years: The usual dose is 2.5 mg (half a tablet or 5 mL of oral solution) once daily in the evening. Children 6 months to 5 years: The usual dose is 1.25 mg (2.5 mL of oral solution) once daily in the evening. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have kidney problems. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions, as doses can vary based on your age, weight, and health condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed one, as this can increase your risk of side effects.
storage: Store levocetirizine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If you have unused or expired medicine, ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking levocetirizine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Be careful driving a car, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness — such as sleeping pills, anti-anxiety medicines, muscle relaxants, or other antihistamines — without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency medical help if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (trouble breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe rash or hives); severe dizziness or fainting; difficulty urinating; fast or irregular heartbeat; or seizures. Also contact your doctor if you have unusual tiredness, confusion, or if your allergy symptoms do not improve after a few days of taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Levocetirizine usually starts relieving allergy symptoms within 1 hour of taking your first dose. It works best when taken regularly at the same time each day. For seasonal or ongoing allergies, you may need to continue taking it throughout the allergy season or as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as drowsiness and dizziness, which can increase the risk of falls. Kidney problems: Your doctor may reduce your dose if your kidneys are not working well, since this medicine is removed from the body by the kidneys. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking levocetirizine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks before recommending this medicine. Children under 6 months: This medicine is not recommended for infants younger than 6 months.
